plan_fit.method: Floors 1-3 (S2-S4, 2000 x 1545 px) are drawn at one scale, 18.25 px/m, with north up: a single offset per image puts the OSM outline of r12122775 on the drawn walls to about +-0.5 m (south face, entrance recess, west/east walls, the neck at x 16.1 / 61.5, the north wing's walls, bumps, stair towers and the curved front all line up). Floor 4 (S5) is a different, schematic drawing at about 29.6 px/m: it was registered on the two stairwells that flank the entrance recess on every floor (x 18.8 and 58.7 at y 258.5) and checked on the west restrooms (x 18.8..24.3 on F2-F4), the main elevator pair (x 28.3..34.6 vs 28.5..35.5 on F1-F3) and the east elevator (x 54.9..58.7 on every floor), all within about 1 m in x; its y positions drift by up to ~2.5 m (the elevator pair), so F4-F6 are +-1.5 m. The plan images were only used for measuring and are not copied into the project.
findings: Floors 1-3 fill the whole OSM footprint: the 1967 south block (80 x 33.5 m with the 4.3 m entrance recess) plus the 2006 north wing (x 6.1..72.0, y 295.9..315.8, the curved glass front to y 320.1 between two stair towers) joined by a 45.5 m wide neck (x 16.1..61.5, y 287.6..295.9).

Floors 4-6 are a narrower tower, about x 11.8..65.3 (53.5 m) by y 258.5..282.8, centred on the entrance axis (38.55 vs 38.9), with small bays on the west (the reading nook) and east and two 3 x 5 m projections that reach the base's north wall. The 2005 photo (S23) shows exactly this: a taller central block on low wings.

The entrance recess (x 19.3..58.3 at y 258.5) runs through floors 1-3 and the tower's middle face stands on the same line; the stairwells flank the recess on every floor (x 18.8..22.1 and 54.9..58.7).

Area check: 3 x 4,364 m2 (F1-F3, OSM) + 3 x the tower plate = about 181,000 sq ft against 177,000 sq ft total (S14); the north wing alone (3 x ~1,857 m2) = ~60,000 sq ft, exactly the 'three-story 60,000 sq ft addition' (S13); the 1967 building (3 x 2,507 m2 base + 3 floors of tower) = ~121,000 sq ft against 117,000-120,000 (S13, S15).

The main elevators (x ~28.5..35.3, y ~271.2..274.4) open NORTH on every floor, into the study areas behind the 1st-floor lobby: this is why the 1st-floor stacks are reached from the 2nd floor (S11) while the lobby (cafe, Starbucks, escalators) is a separate pocket.
The escalators rise north from just inside the revolving door (bottom ~y 261, top ~y 276 on F2); down = west lane, up = east lane (EXIT / up arrows on S3).

sources.title: UF News (2007-01): University of Florida to dedicate Library West on Jan. 26
sources.used_for: opened 1967 as the Graduate Research Library (600,000 volumes, 600 study spaces); reopened August 2006; compact shelving for 1.7 million volumes; 1,400 seats; 20 group study rooms, 84 graduate studies, 36 faculty studies, study booths, a presentation area, a digital media center, two training rooms, a graduate student floor, 139 computers

sources.title: The Independent Florida Alligator (2008-06-30): Library West reopens after mini-makeover
sources.used_for: escalators and elevators on the first, second and third floors (flooring damage around them); the 2006 cork floor replaced by recycled marble and granite chips in the original mustard tone; circulation desk facelift; SelfCheck machines at the desk

sources.title: The Independent Florida Alligator (2011-11-28): finals hours
sources.used_for: floors 1-4 open to any student, floor 5 staff only, floor 6 graduate students with an ID card; the 1st-floor Starbucks keeps library hours; open 8 a.m.-4 a.m. during finals

sources.title: UF News (2012-08-21): Overnight hours at Library West will continue during fall semester
sources.used_for: Library West open 24 hours, five days a week (pilot 2011-12, renewed with Student Government funding) - the 'after dark' premise

sources.title: The Independent Florida Alligator: the Allen H. Neuharth Reading Room + Library West collections page (read through search-result summaries)
sources.used_for: the College of Journalism's news reading room on the 3rd floor of Library West, modelled on the old room, with a big-screen TV streaming live news and local/national newspapers and magazines; the collections page (librarywest.uflib.ufl.edu/services-resources/collections/) puts the newspapers in the Neuharth Reading Room in the south-east corner of the 3rd floor

sources.title: The Independent Florida Alligator (2016-08-01): Library West colonnade and the alligator statue
sources.used_for: the 9-ft bronze alligator (A.H. Burnett Foundation) was then displayed on the 3rd floor of Library West; Starbucks to get an additional exit; about 1.4 million visits a year

sources.title: The Independent Florida Alligator (2025-2026): finals hours (read through search-result summaries)
sources.used_for: Library West and Marston open until 4 a.m. during finals; the Library West Starbucks stays open for the extended hours

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, Category:Library West (photos)
sources.used_for: Dsg_UF_Library_West.jpg (2005-05-07, during the renovation): the plaza face is a taller central block - a two-storey base, then four storeys of vertical brick piers with narrow window slots under a red-tile hipped roof - with low wings either side behind the colonnade; Dsg_UF_Plaza_of_the_Americas_20050507.jpg: the same from across the Plaza; UF-LibraryWest.JPG: the addition's north side - brick gabled pavilions in the Collegiate Gothic manner, a tall arched window, a long glass curtain wall between them

sources.title: UF Libraries Communications (2025-08-15): Longtime library donor's alligator is released on new garden terrace
sources.used_for: the bronze alligator 'Focused Attention' now sits on a limestone base on the new Garden Terrace in front of the colonnade, facing the Plaza (seen through the entrance glass)
